intent: Let an agent confirm elements that only fix wording.

edit.summary:
I made four proposals in the `authoring` domain. All four came back `ok` with 0 issues, and nothing has been confirmed or deployed. I left `delivery` alone.

- **`actions.confirm_wording_element` (new):** An agent can use it to confirm an element, but only if the element is marked `wording_only`. If it isn't, the action is refused with the reason "Only an element that fixes wording alone can be confirmed without a person; confirm the rest as a person." The existing `confirm_element` is unchanged, so it is still person-only and still the route for anything that changes substance.
- **`objects.Element`:** I added an optional `wording_only` boolean fact.
- **`actions.propose_element`:** It takes an optional `wording_only` param and stores it on the element.
- **`transitions.Element`:** The new action goes from `proposed` or `unknown` to `confirmed`, and is not available once an element is confirmed.

The `wording_only` flag is set by whoever proposes the element, so an agent could mark its own proposal as wording-only. I chose this because nothing in the declaration can classify a change as wording-only. If you want an independent check, the kernel would have to set the flag. I didn't try that because I can't see the kernel's interface.

The new action and its two matrix cells are marked `proposed` rather than `confirmed`, since no one has confirmed them yet.
